entries.label: MNE-Python standard_1005 / 1020 montage

entries.notes: MNE's standard_1005 montage ships in fiducial-based 'head' coordinates (not MNI mm), so the app does NOT use it directly for placement. The MNI-mm scalp coordinates in electrodes.json come from the FieldTrip standard_1020 template instead (see standard-1020-electrodes). Kept here as the canonical open 10-20 montage reference.

entries.label: FieldTrip standard_1020 template electrode positions (MNI mm)

entries.source: FieldTrip (Oostenveld et al.) template/electrode/standard_1020.elc
entries.notes: 10-20 SCALP electrode positions already registered to MNI mm: F3 (-50.2, 53.1, 42.2), F4 (51.8, 54.3, 40.8), Fz (0.3, 58.5, 66.5), Cz (0.4, -9.2, 100.2). Only these factual coordinates are used (not FieldTrip's GPL code). NOTE: Okamoto 2004 — often cited for 10-20 MNI coords — reports CORTICAL PROJECTION points, not scalp positions, so it is not used here. Values verified verbatim against the .elc file (2026-06-19).

entries.label: Fox et al. 2012 — sgACC-connectivity DLPFC target
entries.use: Connectivity-based DLPFC preset coordinate
entries.source: Fox, Buckner, White, Greicius & Pascual-Leone 2012, Biological Psychiatry 72(7):595-603 (PMID 22658708; DOI 10.1016/j.biopsych.2012.04.028)
entries.notes: The connectivity preset uses the group-average left-DLPFC peak ANTICORRELATED with the subgenual-ACC seed: MNI (-44, 38, 34) — the paper's own attribution ('the peak anticorrelation in the left DLPFC (-44 38 34, Fig 3A)'). Fox also reports an efficacy-seed optimum at (-38, 44, 26) (Fig. 3B). The sgACC SEED is a 10 mm sphere at (6, 16, -10) — a reference region, NOT a coil target. CORRECTION (verified 2026-06-19, adversarially against the clean PMC HTML full text PMC4120275 where minus signs/table cells render unambiguously): the widely-quoted (-44, 40, 29) is Fox's a-priori 'BA46-center' candidate target (Table 1B), not the connectivity-derived peak, so it is deliberately NOT used. CAVEAT 1 (coordinate space): that (-44, 40, 29) is the MNI conversion of the Rajkowska & Goldman-Rakic 1995 anatomical Talairach coordinate (-44, 40, 25), per Table 1B. CAVEAT 2 (edition): Fox's 2013 follow-up (PMC3594474) re-reports the same subgenual peak as (-42, 38, 34) (x shifted 2 mm); we use the (-44, 38, 34) value verbatim from the 2012 original. Weigand 2018 further refines the optimum to (-42, 44, 30) on an N=1000 connectome — see weigand-2018-connectivity. All are group-average optima; individualized targeting is a separate extension.

entries.label: Fox et al. 2012 — subgenual-ACC (sgACC) connectivity seed coordinate
entries.use: sgACC SEED marker — deep end of the schematic DLPFC→sgACC cue
entries.source: Fox, Buckner, White, Greicius & Pascual-Leone 2012, Biological Psychiatry 72(7):595-603 (PMID 22658708; DOI 10.1016/j.biopsych.2012.04.028)
entries.notes: The subgenual-ACC SEED region behind Fox 2012's connectivity analysis: a 10 mm sphere centred at MNI (6, 16, -10). It is a resting-state REFERENCE region, NOT a coil target and NOT a 10-20 scalp electrode — the connectivity preset stimulates the DLPFC site (-44, 38, 34) most ANTICORRELATED with this seed (see fox-2012-sgacc-target). The optional electrode-marker layer draws it as the deep end of a DLPFC→sgACC cue that is SCHEMATIC / illustrative of that anticorrelation rationale — it is NOT a computed connectome or tractography and carries no quantitative connectivity value. NEVER attribute the seed/electrode targeting to PMID 25922128 (an unrelated tES-sensations paper).

entries.label: Beam et al. 2009 — Beam-F3 localization method
entries.use: F3 (Beam-F3) preset method attribution
entries.source: Beam, Borckardt, Reeves & George 2009, Brain Stimulation 2(1):50-54 (PMID 20539835; DOI 10.1016/j.brs.2008.09.006)
entries.notes: An efficient/accurate method for locating the F3 position for prefrontal TMS from three head measurements (tragus-to-tragus, nasion-to-inion, head circumference) — faster than full 10-20 montaging. Attribute the Beam-F3 scalp heuristic to Beam et al. 2009.

entries.label: Mir-Moghtadaei et al. 2015 — BeamF3 vs MRI-neuronavigated concordance
entries.use: Beam-F3 accuracy claim (targeting explainer)
entries.source: Mir-Moghtadaei, Caballero, Fried et al. 2015, Brain Stimulation 8(5):965-973 (PMID 26115776; DOI 10.1016/j.brs.2015.05.008)
entries.notes: BeamF3-to-MRI-neuronavigated-target discrepancy: <0.65 cm in 50% (MEDIAN), <0.99 cm in 75%, <1.36 cm in 95% of subjects — so 0.65 cm is a median, NOT a hard bound. The MRI-neuronavigated DLPFC target was MNI (-38, +44, +26) (derived by reverse-coregistration from the Fox-suggested optimal target). This is why Beam-F3 lands close to the connectivity target.

entries.label: Weigand et al. 2018 — N=1000 sgACC-connectivity target refinement
entries.use: Connectivity preset refinement note
entries.source: Weigand, Horn, Caballero et al. 2018, Biological Psychiatry 84(1):28-37 (PMID 29274805; DOI 10.1016/j.biopsych.2017.10.028)
entries.notes: Prospective validation that subgenual connectivity predicts TMS antidepressant efficacy. Using an N=1000 normative connectome, the peak subgenual-anticorrelation in left DLPFC was MNI (-42, 44, 30) — between Fox 2012's two reported peaks (-44, 38, 34) and (-38, 44, 26). Group-average optimum.

entries.label: 5-cm rule misses DLPFC (Herwig 2001; Trapp 2020)
entries.use: 5-cm-rule deprecated-method explainer
entries.source: Herwig, Padberg, Unger, Spitzer & Schonfeldt-Lecuona 2001, Biological Psychiatry 50(1):58-61 (PMID 11457424; DOI 10.1016/s0006-3223(01)01153-2)
entries.notes: The standard 5-cm method correctly targeted DLPFC (BA9) in only 7 of 22 subjects (31.8%); in 15/22 (68.2%) the coil landed more dorsally (e.g. premotor) — i.e. it misses the DLPFC in well over 1/3 of patients (the >1/3 claim is conservative). Ignores head size: the true DLPFC sits ~7 cm (not 5 cm) anterior to the motor hotspot (Ahdab 2010, PMID 20230933). The 5.5-cm-rule cortical target is MNI (-33.6, 30.8, 51.1) and Beam-F3's cortical projection is (-40.6, 41.7, 34.3) (Trapp et al. 2020, Brain Stimulation 13(3):578-581, PMID 32289680).

entries.label: Mutz et al. 2019 — network meta-analysis
entries.use: Dose–response RESPONSE odds ratios vs sham by protocol
entries.source: Mutz, Vipulananthan, Carter, Hurlemann, Fu & Young 2019, BMJ 364:l1079 (PMID 30917990; PMCID PMC6435996; DOI 10.1136/bmj.l1079)
entries.notes: RESPONSE odds ratios vs sham (the panel uses HF-L, LF-R, iTBS): high-frequency LEFT rTMS 3.17 (95% CI 2.29–4.37); low-frequency RIGHT rTMS 3.65 (2.13–6.24); intermittent theta-burst stimulation 3.20 (1.45–7.08). (For context: bilateral rTMS 4.92; tDCS 2.65; bitemporal ECT 8.91.) CORRECTION (verified 2026-06-20 verbatim against the open-access Europe PMC deposit PMC6435996): the model is FREQUENTIST multivariate random-effects (REML), so these are 95% CONFIDENCE intervals, NOT Bayesian credible intervals. Primary outcome = RESPONSE, 'defined in most trials as a 50% or greater reduction in depressive symptoms at primary treatment endpoint' (HDRS preferred when both HDRS & MADRS reported); ITT / modified-ITT preferred over completers. Sham arms were merged into ONE reference node, so the paper gives no single sham absolute rate — convert ORs to probabilities against a SEPARATELY-sourced, labeled sham baseline (see berlim-2014-sham), never plotting ORs and raw percentages on one axis (DESIGN §4, gate (c)). Per-protocol remission ORs live in the supplementary appendix (not the main text) and are not used here.

entries.label: THREE-D (Blumberger et al. 2018)
entries.use: iTBS vs 10 Hz absolute response/remission rates
entries.source: Blumberger, Vila-Rodriguez, Thorpe, et al. 2018, Lancet 391(10131):1683-1692 (PMID 29726344; DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(18)30295-2)
entries.notes: Head-to-head non-inferiority RCT (NO sham arm). VERIFIED 2026-06-20 (PubMed abstract + corroborating Table-2 readings): iTBS response 49% (exact 49.2%, 95/193), remission 32% (31.6%, 61/193); 10 Hz response 47% (47.4%, 91/192), remission 27% (26.6%, 51/192). Scale = 17-item HRSD; response = ≥50% HRSD-17 reduction; remission = HRSD-17 < 8. IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS vs the earlier seed: (1) these are PER-PROTOCOL among ASSESSED participants (denominators 192/193), NOT intention-to-treat over the 205/209 randomised; (2) they are the 4–6-week primary-completion-point rates, NOT a 12-week post-treatment timepoint. These are absolute within-arm rates — never an odds ratio and never relative to sham.

entries.label: Berlim et al. 2014 — HF-rTMS meta-analysis
entries.use: HF-rTMS absolute response/remission rates + sham arms
entries.source: Berlim, van den Eynde, Tovar-Perdomo & Daskalakis 2014, Psychological Medicine 44(2):225-239 (PMID 23507264; DOI 10.1017/S0033291713000512)
entries.notes: Meta-analysis of 29 randomised, double-blind, sham-controlled HF-rTMS trials (N=1371; ~13 sessions). VERIFIED 2026-06-20 verbatim against the abstract: active HF-rTMS 29.3% response / 18.6% remission, 'compared with 10.4% and 5% of those receiving sham rTMS'; pooled OR 3.3 (p<0.0001) for both response and remission (NNT 6 and 8). Response = ≥50% reduction on HAM-D/HDRS or MADRS; remission cut-offs were heterogeneous across studies (HAM-D/HDRS ≤7 in most, ≤8 or ≤10 in a few; MADRS <10 in one) — treat the exact cut-off as medium-confidence (paywalled full text). The SHAM arms here are the sham baseline used for OR→probability conversion — see berlim-2014-sham. (Sham '5%' is printed without a decimal — no false precision.)

entries.label: Berlim et al. 2014 — pooled SHAM response/remission baseline
entries.use: Explicit, labeled sham baseline p0 for OR→probability conversion (DESIGN §4)
entries.source: Berlim, van den Eynde, Tovar-Perdomo & Daskalakis 2014, Psychological Medicine 44(2):225-239 (PMID 23507264; DOI 10.1017/S0033291713000512), sham arms
entries.notes: Sham (placebo) baseline used as p0 in the panel's OR→probability conversion: RESPONSE p0 = 10.4%, REMISSION p0 = 5% — the pooled sham-arm proportions from the same 29 sham-controlled RCTs ('compared with 10.4% and 5% of those receiving sham rTMS'; verified 2026-06-20). Internally matched to Berlim's own OR (3.3), so it is an appropriate, sham-referenced p0 for the Mutz 2019 ORs (also sham-referenced). NOT used: Razza et al. 2018 (PMID 29111404) reports placebo response only as a continuous Hedges' g (0.8), not a dichotomous rate, so it cannot serve as a p0.

entries.label: Cole et al. 2022 — Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy (SNT) RCT
entries.use: Accelerated-protocol context — sham-controlled RCT (separate callout)
entries.source: Cole, Phillips, Bentzley, et al. 2022, American Journal of Psychiatry 179(2):132-141 (PMID 34711062; DOI 10.1176/appi.ajp.2021.20101429)
entries.notes: Double-blind sham-controlled RCT of accelerated fMRI-guided iTBS (90,000 pulses / 5 days), MADRS-based (remission = MADRS ≤10, response = ≥50% MADRS reduction). VERIFIED 2026-06-20: remission 78.6% (11/14) active vs 13.3% (2/15) sham; response 85.7% (12/14) vs 26.7% (4/15); primary continuous outcome mean % MADRS reduction 52.5% active vs 11.1% sham at 4 weeks. CAVEATS: very small n=29, STOPPED at a planned interim (effect likely inflated); the categorical rates are CUMULATIVE 'achieved in ≥1 of 5 post-treatment assessments across the 4-week window', NOT single-timepoint (point-prevalence remission immediately post-treatment ≈57%); 4-week durability only; a larger replication (Kratter, World Psychiatry 2026, n=48) reports a more modest ~50% vs ~21% remission. Surfaced QUARANTINED — never folded into the standard-protocol comparison, never an OR, never a sham baseline. The ~90% headline is the open-label pilot, not this RCT — see cole-2020-saint-pilot.

entries.label: Cole et al. 2020 — SAINT open-label pilot
entries.use: Accelerated-protocol context — uncontrolled open-label pilot (separate callout)
entries.source: Cole, Stimpson, Bentzley, et al. 2020, American Journal of Psychiatry 177(8):716-726 (PMID 32252538; DOI 10.1176/appi.ajp.2019.19070720)
entries.notes: SINGLE-ARM, UNCONTROLLED open-label pilot of accelerated fMRI-guided iTBS (SAINT). VERIFIED 2026-06-20: remission (MADRS <11, i.e. ≤10) 90.5% (19/21) completer / 86.4% (19/22) intent-to-treat. This is the source of the often-quoted ~90% remission figure — it has NO sham arm and must NEVER be shown as sham-adjusted or as an odds ratio. Shown only as labeled experimental context.

entries.label: Deng, Lisanby & Peterchev 2013 — TMS depth–focality tradeoff
entries.use: Figure-8 calibration sanity-check for the analytical E-field solver (half-value depth, focality)
entries.source: Deng, Lisanby & Peterchev 2013, Brain Stimulation 6(1):1–13 (doi:10.1016/j.brs.2012.02.005)
entries.notes: Figure-8 half-value depth d½ ≈ 0.9–3.4 cm (radial distance from the cortical surface to the deepest point where E = ½ of its cortical-surface max) and focality S½ down to ≈5 cm² (defined as V½/d½, an area-EQUIVALENT, not a planar contour). The solver's measured d½ ≈ 11 mm sits in this band. CAVEAT (verified): Deng 2013 reports NORMALIZED fields and gives NO absolute V/m; absolute field estimates from other dosimetry must not be presented as outputs of this model. The solver outputs RELATIVE units only (gate (e)) — these ranges are sanity anchors, not solver outputs. The depth–dose readout surfaces this d½ (and an on-surface half-max spread S½) as the coil is tilted / stood off — illustrative, relative, never validated cm.

entries.label: Stokes et al. 2005 — coil-to-cortex distance vs stimulator output
entries.use: Context for the depth–dose readout: coil-to-cortex distance and required stimulator output (no output calculator)
entries.source: Stokes, Chambers, Gould, Henderson, Janko, Allen & Mattingley 2005, Journal of Neurophysiology 94(6):4520-4527 (PMID 16135552; DOI 10.1152/jn.00067.2005)
entries.notes: Motor-cortex study: increasing coil-to-cortex distance required additional stimulator output to maintain equivalent stimulation. This is a compensatory motor-threshold relationship, not a decreasing delivered-output percentage. Cited as context only; no machine-output calculator is implemented. The app’s 0.32 mm/degree tilt lift is an authored heuristic, not derived from this study or Deng.

entries.label: Bungert et al. 2017 — induced-field direction / orientation dependence
entries.use: E-field DIRECTION glyphs — orientation dependence of the TMS effect
entries.source: Bungert, Antunes, Espenhahn & Thielscher 2017, Cerebral Cortex 27(11):5083 (DOI 10.1093/cercor/bhw292)
entries.notes: "Where does TMS Stimulate the Motor Cortex?" — combines TMS electrophysiology with realistic SimNIBS field estimates to localize the affected cortex. Cited for the direction glyphs: the induced field's ORIENTATION relative to cortical (gyral/sulcal) geometry co-determines which neural elements are engaged, so direction — not just magnitude — matters for the effect. NUANCE: the paper's HEADLINE result is that gyral-crown field STRENGTH best predicts the affected position; it nonetheless establishes strong orientation dependence (corroborated by Janssen 2015; Souza 2024). Used ONLY to justify showing field DIRECTION in relative units — the glyphs are constant-length and explicitly NOT a model of neural activation (gate (e)).

entries.label: Google Research 'Turbo' colormap — improved rainbow, not perceptually uniform
entries.use: Methods colour-scale note: why Turbo is offered but kept off-default and not called colour-blind-safe
entries.source: Mikhailov, 'Turbo, An Improved Rainbow Colormap for Visualization', Google AI Blog, 2019
entries.notes: Turbo is a smoother rainbow map (a drop-in jet replacement) tuned for high contrast. The post is explicit that, unlike viridis, it is NOT perceptually uniform — equal steps in value are not equal steps in perceived lightness — so it can exaggerate or hide gradients. Used here ONLY to justify keeping turbo optional/off-default and to avoid claiming it is colour-blind-safe (gate (e): the field stays in relative units regardless of colormap).

entries.label: Nuñez, Anderton & Renslow 2018 — cividis CVD-optimised colormap
entries.use: Methods colour-scale note: cividis as a perceptually-uniform, colour-vision-deficiency-optimised option
entries.source: Nuñez, Anderton & Renslow 2018, PLOS ONE 13(7):e0199239 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0199239)
entries.notes: Introduces cividis: a perceptually-uniform sequential colormap optimised so that viewers with the common colour-vision deficiencies (deuteranopia/protanopia) perceive the same data ordering as trichromats (near-isoluminant in the red–green channel). Cited for offering cividis as the CVD-friendly heatmap option; it maps the same relative-units field as viridis/turbo (gate (e)).
